group_assessment.weighting: A clinical genetics group reporting two consanguineous families with commercial-laboratory WES and Sanger confirmation. The observation (genotype, segregation in family 1, phenotype) is weighted as a case report; the interpretation (splice consequence, the 'one functional copy is sufficient' sentence, the review table) carries no experimental weight and the review table contains transcription errors, so it is not used as a source for any other paper's allele.

entries.proposition: ALLELE CLASS / ZYGOSITY / SEGREGATION, family 1: a homozygous canonical splice-donor variant (intron 4, +1) found by WES; both parents and an unaffected sister are reported heterozygous carriers. The carrier phenotype is the authors' word 'healthy', not an examination.
entries.snippet: Whole exome sequencing (WES) revealed novel homozygous variant in intron 4 of the WWOX gene, NM_016373.3: c.409+1G > T (Ch16:78149052 G>T). Parents and healthy sister tested and they are carrier for the same mutation.
entries.anchor: Result, first clinical report (family 1 proband), final sentences

entries.proposition: PHENOTYPE BAND, family 1 proband: onset at two months with focal seizures evolving to infantile spasms, refractory; a DEE band.
entries.snippet: At two months he started to have focal seizure with secondary generalization followed by infantile spasms. The seizure was refractory to antiepileptic medications.

entries.proposition: NO RNA OR FUNCTIONAL TEST of the splice allele: its consequence is stated as a possibility only.
entries.snippet: This mutation might cause intron sequence to be included in the mRNA or the elimination of exon.

entries.proposition: ALLELE CLASS / ZYGOSITY, family 2: two affected siblings homozygous for the previously reported nonsense allele p.Arg54*; the paper reports no parental testing for this family.
entries.snippet: WES revealed previously reported homozygous non sense mutation c.160G > T (p.Arg54*), which resulted in a premature termination.
entries.anchor: Result, third clinical report (family 2, second affected sib)

entries.proposition: PHENOTYPE BAND, family 2 index: early spasms with burst suppression on EEG; severe DEE band.
entries.snippet: electroencephalogram (EEG) low voltage interval with burst suppression

entries.proposition: THE AUTHORS' HAPLOSUFFICIENCY SENTENCE is an inference from the zygosity of reported cases, not a measurement; and it states 'all homozygous' while the same paper's Table 1 lists a compound heterozygote (see next entry).
entries.snippet: All of these mutations are homozygous and most of them are located in or near the first WW domain, suggesting that one functional copy of the WWOX gene is sufficient for conducting normal neuronal activity.

entries.proposition: INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: Table 1 itself records a compound heterozygote among the reviewed cases.
entries.snippet: Compound heterozygous for both mutations in trans configuration

entries.proposition: TRANSCRIPTION ERROR IN THE REVIEW TABLE: the Johannsen 2018 allele is printed as a glycine-230 change with a reversed nucleotide arrow. Genotype caution: this secondary table must not be used as a source for the Q230P allele.
entries.snippet: (a) Might cause intron insertion or exon skipping (b) p.Arg54* p.Gly230Pro
entries.anchor: Table 1, row 'Amino acid change', first two study columns (this study; the 2018 Q230P report)

entries.proposition: Figure 1 inspected: sagittal and axial MRI of the family-2 sister show a thin corpus callosum, volume loss and asymmetric ventricular enlargement, as the legend states.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1, three panels A-C: sagittal T1 with arrow on a thin corpus callosum; axial T2 and T1 with red arrows on reduced white matter and a star in an enlarged left lateral ventricle.
